questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: According to the Genesis creation account, God created the world in
options: one single day
seven days, resting on the eighth
six days, resting on the seventh
forty days and forty nights
questions.explanation: Genesis 1-2 recounts God completing the work of creation in six days and resting on the seventh, which became the basis for the Sabbath.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: According to Genesis, the first man and woman created by God were
options: Abraham and Sarah
Noah and his wife
Adam and Eve
Isaac and Rebekah
questions.explanation: Genesis identifies Adam and Eve as the first human beings created by God, placed in the Garden of Eden.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: In the account of the Fall, Adam and Eve disobeyed God by
options: refusing to name the animals
building an altar without God's instruction
eating the forbidden fruit from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil
leaving the Garden of Eden without permission
questions.explanation: Genesis 3 describes Adam and Eve's disobedience in eating fruit from the one tree God had explicitly forbidden them to eat from, resulting in the Fall.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: As a direct consequence of the Fall, God pronounced punishment that included
options: pain in childbirth for the woman and toil in labour for the man
the destruction of the entire earth by flood
the confusion of human languages
immediate physical death for both Adam and Eve
questions.explanation: God's judgement in Genesis 3 included increased pain in childbirth for Eve and difficult, toilsome labour on the cursed ground for Adam, along with their expulsion from Eden.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The sovereignty of God, as illustrated in the early narratives of Genesis, refers to God's
options: dependence on human permission before acting
limited influence confined only to the nation of Israel
supreme power and authority over all creation and human affairs
absence from the affairs of the created world
questions.explanation: God's sovereignty is demonstrated throughout Genesis as His ultimate authority and control over creation, human history, and the unfolding of His purposes.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Joseph, one of the sons of Jacob, rose to a position of leadership in Egypt mainly through his ability to
options: build the pyramids of Egypt
translate foreign languages for Pharaoh's court
interpret dreams, including Pharaoh's dreams about the coming famine
lead Egypt's army into successful battles
questions.explanation: Joseph's God-given gift of dream interpretation, especially of Pharaoh's dreams predicting seven years of plenty followed by seven years of famine, led to his elevation to a position of great authority in Egypt.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Joseph's brothers initially mistreated him mainly out of
options: anger at Joseph's disobedience to their father
a shared decision by their father to punish Joseph
fear that Joseph would leave the family permanently
jealousy over their father's favouritism and Joseph's dreams of ruling over them
questions.explanation: Joseph's brothers resented him for Jacob's evident favouritism (symbolised by the coat of many colours) and for his dreams suggesting he would one day rule over them, leading them to sell him into slavery.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Moses was chosen by God to lead the Israelites out of slavery in
options: Canaan
Assyria
Babylon
Egypt
questions.explanation: Moses is the central figure in the Exodus narrative, called by God to lead the enslaved Israelites out of bondage in Egypt to the promised land.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: God first called Moses to his leadership mission through the appearance of
options: a pillar of cloud by day
a rainbow in the sky
a burning bush that was not consumed by the fire
a dream during the night
questions.explanation: In Exodus 3, God appears to Moses in a bush that burns without being consumed, calling him to lead the Israelites out of Egypt.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: After the death of Moses, God appointed which leader to lead the Israelites into the Promised Land?
options: Joshua
Aaron
Samson
Gideon
questions.explanation: Joshua succeeded Moses as the leader of the Israelites, tasked with leading them across the Jordan River into the land of Canaan.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Under Joshua's leadership, the famous walls of which city collapsed after the Israelites marched around it?
options: Bethlehem
Jericho
Nazareth
Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Following God's specific instructions, the Israelites marched around Jericho for seven days, after which its walls miraculously collapsed, allowing them to conquer the city.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Gideon, one of the judges of Israel, is best known for
options: defeating a much larger Midianite army with only 300 chosen men
building the first temple in Jerusalem
writing the book of Psalms
leading the Israelites out of Egyptian slavery
questions.explanation: Gideon, guided by God, reduced his army to just 300 men to demonstrate that Israel's victory over the Midianites came through God's power, not human strength.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Before agreeing to lead Israel against the Midianites, Gideon sought confirmation from God through the sign of
options: a rainbow in the sky
a fleece of wool that became wet or dry as he requested
the parting of the Red Sea
a burning bush
questions.explanation: Gideon asked God for confirmation using a wool fleece, requesting it be wet with dew while the ground remained dry, and then the reverse, to be certain of God's call.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Samson, another judge of Israel, was famous for his
options: leadership of Israel's priesthood
extraordinary physical strength, given by God through his Nazarite vow
skill in building the temple
wisdom in settling legal disputes
questions.explanation: Samson possessed supernatural physical strength tied to his Nazarite vow, a key part of which was never cutting his hair, and which he used against Israel's enemies, the Philistines.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Samson's strength was ultimately compromised when
options: he broke his vow by touching a dead body
he grew old and naturally weak
Delilah discovered the secret of his strength lay in his uncut hair and had it cut while he slept
he lost a wrestling match to a Philistine soldier
questions.explanation: Delilah persistently pressed Samson until he revealed the true secret of his strength, allowing the Philistines to cut his hair while he slept and capture him.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The period of the Judges in Israel's history was generally characterised by
options: a repeating cycle of Israel's disobedience, oppression by enemies, repentance, and deliverance by a judge
a stable, centralised monarchy under a single king
complete abandonment of the worship of God by all Israelites
peaceful, uninterrupted prosperity with no conflict
questions.explanation: The Book of Judges describes a recurring cycle: Israel turns from God, is oppressed by enemies, cries out in repentance, and God raises up a judge to deliver them, only for the cycle to repeat.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Saul, the first king of Israel, was anointed by the prophet
options: Nathan
Isaiah
Samuel
Elijah
questions.explanation: The prophet Samuel anointed Saul as the first king of Israel at the people's request for a king like other nations.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Saul's disobedience to God, which ultimately cost him God's favour, involved
options: abandoning his throne voluntarily
offering a sacrifice himself instead of waiting for Samuel, and later failing to fully destroy the Amalekites as commanded
refusing to fight against the Philistines at all
building an idol for the Israelites to worship
questions.explanation: Saul's repeated disobedience, including impatiently offering a sacrifice reserved for Samuel and sparing King Agag and the best of the Amalekite livestock against God's explicit command, led to his rejection as king.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: David, who succeeded Saul as king, first gained public recognition for
options: defeating the Philistine giant Goliath in single combat
writing the entire book of Proverbs
leading the Israelites out of Egypt
building the first temple in Jerusalem
questions.explanation: David's victory over the giant Goliath, using only a sling and stones, brought him to national prominence and marked the beginning of his rise to kingship.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: David's rise to kingship was complicated by the jealousy and hostility of
options: his own father, Jesse
the prophet Samuel, who opposed his anointing
the Philistine king, Achish
King Saul, who repeatedly sought to kill him
questions.explanation: Despite David's loyal service, Saul grew increasingly jealous of David's popularity and military success, repeatedly attempting to kill him before David eventually became king.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: A major moral failure in David's life as king involved
options: his refusal to ever fight in battle
his abandonment of the worship of God entirely
his decision to divide the kingdom of Israel
his adultery with Bathsheba and the arranged death of her husband, Uriah
questions.explanation: David's affair with Bathsheba, followed by his arrangement to have her husband Uriah killed in battle to cover up the resulting pregnancy, stands as one of the most serious moral failures recorded of him.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Solomon, David's son and successor, is best known for his
options: role as a judge of Israel before the monarchy
exceptional wisdom, granted to him by God, and for building the first Temple in Jerusalem
military conquests across foreign lands
leadership of the Israelites during the Exodus
questions.explanation: Solomon famously asked God for wisdom to govern Israel well, and used his wealth and wisdom to construct the first Temple in Jerusalem as a permanent house of worship.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Despite his wisdom, Solomon's later reign was marked by a moral and spiritual lapse involving
options: his abandonment of Jerusalem as the capital
his many foreign wives leading him into the worship of other gods
his rejection of all wealth and possessions
his complete refusal to build the Temple
questions.explanation: In his later years, Solomon's numerous foreign wives influenced him to build shrines and participate in the worship of foreign gods, a serious departure from exclusive devotion to God.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The famous judgement in which Solomon proposed dividing a disputed baby in two to determine its true mother demonstrated his
options: skill in temple architecture
wisdom in discerning truth and justice
ability to interpret dreams
military strategy in warfare
questions.explanation: Solomon's clever proposal revealed the true mother, who begged for the baby's life to be spared rather than divided, showcasing the divine wisdom Solomon had been granted.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: After Solomon's death, the kingdom of Israel was divided mainly due to
options: an agreement between Solomon's sons to rule jointly
a foreign invasion that split the territory
the harsh policies of his son Rehoboam, which led the northern tribes to rebel
a natural disaster separating the north from the south
questions.explanation: Rehoboam's refusal to lighten the heavy burdens imposed by Solomon led the ten northern tribes to rebel and form the separate Kingdom of Israel, while Judah remained loyal to the Davidic line in the south.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Following the division of the kingdom, the northern kingdom retained the name
options: Judah
Babylon
Israel
Assyria
questions.explanation: After the split following Solomon's reign, the ten northern tribes formed the Kingdom of Israel, while the southern tribes formed the Kingdom of Judah.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: King Ahab of Israel is particularly remembered for his idolatrous worship promoted through his wife
options: Rebekah, the wife of Isaac
Delilah, who betrayed Samson
Jezebel, who promoted the worship of Baal
Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah
questions.explanation: Ahab's marriage to the Phoenician princess Jezebel led to widespread promotion of Baal worship in Israel, a central conflict in the narratives involving the prophet Elijah.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The prophet Elijah famously confronted the prophets of Baal in a dramatic contest on
options: Mount of Olives
Mount Carmel
Mount Sinai
Mount Horeb only
questions.explanation: On Mount Carmel, Elijah challenged the prophets of Baal to a contest to call down fire from heaven, decisively demonstrating the power of the God of Israel over Baal.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: After his victory over the prophets of Baal, Elijah fled into the wilderness in fear of
options: an approaching foreign army
King Ahab's direct attack
a severe famine in the land
Queen Jezebel's threat to kill him
questions.explanation: Despite his triumphant victory on Mount Carmel, Elijah fled in fear after Jezebel vowed to have him killed in retaliation for the deaths of her prophets.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The prophet Amos is particularly known for his messages concerning
options: the rebuilding of the Jerusalem Temple
the coming birth of the Messiah
social justice and condemnation of the exploitation of the poor
the reign of King Solomon
questions.explanation: Amos's prophetic ministry strongly emphasised social justice, sharply condemning the wealthy for exploiting and oppressing the poor and vulnerable in Israelite society.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The prophet Hosea's own difficult marriage to an unfaithful wife was used symbolically to represent
options: the friendship between David and Jonathan
the political alliance between Israel and Judah
Israel's unfaithfulness to God despite His enduring love and covenant faithfulness
the reconciliation between Jacob and Esau
questions.explanation: Hosea's painful marital experience became a living illustration of Israel's spiritual unfaithfulness to God, while also demonstrating God's persistent, faithful love in seeking reconciliation.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The prophet Isaiah's call to prophetic ministry is described as occurring through a vision of
options: God's glory in the Temple, attended by seraphim
a lion's den
a valley filled with dry bones
a burning bush in the wilderness
questions.explanation: Isaiah chapter 6 describes his dramatic vision of God's holiness and glory in the Temple, attended by seraphim, following which he responds to God's call to be sent as a prophet.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Jeremiah's Temple Sermon warned the people of Judah that
options: God had abandoned Judah completely with no hope of restoration
their empty religious rituals would not protect them from judgement if they continued in disobedience and injustice
foreign nations would never threaten Jerusalem
the Temple would stand forever regardless of the people's behaviour
questions.explanation: In his Temple Sermon (Jeremiah 7), Jeremiah warned that the people's false confidence in the Temple's presence would not shield them from judgement if they persisted in injustice and idolatry.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Jeremiah is often referred to as the 'weeping prophet' mainly because of his
options: physical blindness throughout his ministry
constant conflict with King David
deep sorrow over Judah's persistent sin and the coming judgement he was called to announce
personal poverty and homelessness
questions.explanation: Jeremiah's prophetic ministry was marked by profound personal grief over the sins of his people and the painful judgement he foresaw and had to proclaim, earning him this well-known title.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Which prophet is most closely associated with warnings and messages directed at the northern kingdom of Israel, particularly concerning social injustice, alongside Amos?
options: Jeremiah
Ezekiel
Hosea
Isaiah
questions.explanation: Hosea, like Amos, prophesied primarily to the northern kingdom of Israel, though his focus centred more on Israel's spiritual unfaithfulness to God, illustrated through his own marriage.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The prophets of the divided kingdom period, such as Amos, Hosea, Isaiah, and Jeremiah, generally shared a common message calling the people to
options: military conquest of neighbouring nations
the construction of new pagan temples
the abolition of the monarchy entirely
repentance, social justice, and renewed faithfulness to God
questions.explanation: Despite their different individual circumstances, these prophets consistently called Israel and Judah back to covenant faithfulness, genuine worship, and social justice.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Ezekiel's vision of the valley of dry bones symbolised
options: the creation of the world by God
the crossing of the Red Sea by the Israelites
the future restoration and revival of Israel from its spiritual and national death in exile
the final destruction of Israel with no hope of restoration
questions.explanation: Ezekiel's vision (Ezekiel 37) of dry bones coming to life symbolised God's promise to restore and revive the nation of Israel, even after the devastation of exile.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Ezekiel ministered as a prophet primarily to the Israelites during their
options: wandering in the wilderness after the Exodus
exile in Babylon
return from exile under Nehemiah
settlement in the Promised Land under Joshua
questions.explanation: Ezekiel prophesied among the Jewish exiles living in Babylon following the fall of Jerusalem, offering both warnings and messages of future hope and restoration.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Daniel demonstrated his unwavering faith in God most famously by
options: surviving unharmed after being thrown into a den of lions for continuing to pray to God
interpreting the Ten Commandments for the exiles
building the second Temple in Jerusalem
leading the Israelites in battle against Babylon
questions.explanation: Daniel's steadfast commitment to praying to God, despite a royal decree forbidding it, led to his being thrown into a lions' den, from which God miraculously delivered him unharmed.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Daniel and his three friends first demonstrated their faithfulness to God while in Babylon by
options: refusing to learn the Babylonian language
leaving Babylon without royal permission
rebuilding the Temple in Jerusalem
refusing to eat the king's rich food and wine, choosing vegetables and water instead
questions.explanation: Daniel and his companions chose to maintain their religious dietary convictions by requesting simple food, trusting God rather than the richer provisions of the Babylonian royal table.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Nehemiah is best known in the Old Testament for his role in
options: leading the Israelites out of Egyptian slavery
defeating the Philistines with 300 men
building the first Temple in Jerusalem
leading the rebuilding of the walls of Jerusalem after the exile
questions.explanation: Nehemiah, serving as governor, organised and led the successful rebuilding of Jerusalem's broken walls after the Jewish exiles began returning from Babylon.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Nehemiah faced significant opposition to the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls from enemies such as
options: Saul and the Philistines
Pharaoh and his army
Ahab and Jezebel
Sanballat and Tobiah
questions.explanation: Nehemiah's rebuilding efforts were persistently opposed and mocked by local officials Sanballat and Tobiah, who attempted to intimidate and sabotage the work.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The period of Exile and Return in Old Testament history primarily involved the Israelites being taken captive to and later returning from
options: Assyria only
Egypt
Babylon
Rome
questions.explanation: Following the fall of Jerusalem, the people of Judah were taken into exile in Babylon, from which they later began to return under leaders such as Ezra and Nehemiah.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: A key theological lesson emphasised through the Exile and Return narratives (Ezekiel, Daniel, Nehemiah) is that
options: God permanently abandoned Israel with no possibility of restoration
the Israelites achieved their restoration entirely through their own military strength
God remains faithful to His people and can restore them even after judgement, provided they remain faithful to Him
exile was a purely political event with no spiritual significance
questions.explanation: These narratives collectively emphasise that even amid judgement and exile, God remains faithful to His covenant promises, offering restoration to those who remain faithful to Him.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: According to the Gospels, Jesus was born in the town of
options: Jerusalem
Nazareth
Bethlehem
Capernaum
questions.explanation: The Gospels of Matthew and Luke record that Jesus was born in Bethlehem, fulfilling Old Testament prophecy concerning the birthplace of the Messiah.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Jesus was baptised in the Jordan River by
options: John the Baptist
Paul
Andrew
Peter
questions.explanation: John the Baptist baptised Jesus in the Jordan River, an event marked by the Holy Spirit descending like a dove and a voice from heaven affirming Jesus as God's Son.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Immediately after His baptism, Jesus was led by the Spirit into the wilderness, where He
options: began His public ministry immediately
performed His first miracle
called His first disciples
was tempted by the devil for forty days
questions.explanation: Following His baptism, Jesus spent forty days fasting in the wilderness, during which He faced and overcame temptation from the devil.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: During His temptation in the wilderness, Jesus resisted the devil's temptations mainly by
options: calling on the angels for immediate rescue
quoting Scripture in response to each temptation
performing a miracle to prove His power
arguing philosophically with the devil
questions.explanation: In each of the three temptations recorded, Jesus responded by quoting Old Testament Scripture, demonstrating reliance on God's word rather than succumbing to the devil's offers.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Transfiguration of Jesus, witnessed by Peter, James, and John, involved
options: Jesus's appearance being radically changed to shine with divine glory, accompanied by Moses and Elijah
Jesus walking on water before His disciples
Jesus calming a violent storm at sea
Jesus raising Lazarus from the dead
questions.explanation: At the Transfiguration, Jesus's appearance was gloriously transformed on a mountain, and He was seen conversing with Moses and Elijah, affirming His divine identity to the three witnessing disciples.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: At the Transfiguration, a voice from a cloud declared concerning Jesus,
options: 'Behold the Lamb of God'
'This is my beloved Son; listen to him'
'It is finished'
'This is the King of the Jews'
questions.explanation: The divine voice at the Transfiguration echoed the declaration made at Jesus's baptism, affirming His identity as God's beloved Son and commanding the disciples to listen to Him.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The birth of Jesus was announced to the shepherds by
options: the wise men from the East
the Roman emperor Caesar Augustus
King Herod directly
an angel, accompanied by a heavenly host praising God
questions.explanation: Luke's Gospel records that an angel appeared to shepherds in the fields near Bethlehem to announce the birth of Jesus, followed by a multitude of the heavenly host praising God.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: According to Matthew's Gospel, wise men (Magi) from the East came to worship the infant Jesus, guided by
options: a dream alone, with no other guide
a message from King Herod
an angelic vision only
a star
questions.explanation: Matthew's Gospel describes the wise men following a star that led them to the place where the young child Jesus was, where they presented gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: King Herod's reaction to the news of the birth of a 'King of the Jews' was to
options: send gifts of gold and silver to the newborn Jesus
immediately abdicate his throne
order the massacre of infant boys in Bethlehem in an attempt to eliminate this perceived rival
welcome Jesus as the legitimate future king
questions.explanation: Threatened by the news of a newborn 'King of the Jews', Herod ordered the killing of infant boys in and around Bethlehem, though Jesus's family had already fled to Egypt to escape this danger.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Holy Spirit's descent upon Jesus at His baptism took the visible form of
options: tongues of fire
a rainbow
a bright star
a dove
questions.explanation: All four Gospels describe the Holy Spirit descending on Jesus at His baptism in the visible form of a dove, confirming His anointing for ministry.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Jesus's triumphal entry into Jerusalem, marking the beginning of Passion Week, involved Him riding on
options: a donkey
a chariot
a camel
a war horse
questions.explanation: Jesus entered Jerusalem riding on a donkey, fulfilling Old Testament prophecy and symbolising His humble, peaceful kingship, as crowds welcomed Him with palm branches.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: During the Last Supper, Jesus instituted what has become known in Christian practice as
options: the Feast of Tabernacles
Holy Communion (the Lord's Supper)
the Sabbath observance
the rite of baptism
questions.explanation: At the Last Supper, Jesus shared bread and wine with His disciples, instituting the practice of Holy Communion as a remembrance of His body and blood given for them.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Jesus was betrayed to the religious authorities by one of His own twelve disciples, named
options: Peter
Thomas
Judas Iscariot
John
questions.explanation: Judas Iscariot betrayed Jesus to the chief priests for thirty pieces of silver, identifying Him with a kiss in the Garden of Gethsemane.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: In the Garden of Gethsemane, Jesus prayed in deep anguish, asking that, if possible,
options: His ministry be extended for many more years
His disciples be arrested in His place
the cup of suffering before Him be taken away, while submitting to God's will
the Roman authorities be immediately overthrown
questions.explanation: In Gethsemane, Jesus expressed profound distress, asking God to remove the coming suffering if possible, yet ultimately submitting to God's will above His own.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Jesus was crucified at a place called
options: Mount Sinai
Golgotha (the place of the skull)
Mount Carmel
the Garden of Eden
questions.explanation: Jesus was crucified at Golgotha, meaning 'the place of the skull', located just outside Jerusalem.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: According to the Gospels, Jesus was crucified under the authority of the Roman governor
options: Herod Antipas alone
Caiaphas the High Priest
Pontius Pilate
Caesar Augustus directly
questions.explanation: Pontius Pilate, the Roman governor of Judea, ultimately authorised Jesus's crucifixion, despite initially finding no legal basis for the charges against Him.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: According to the Gospel accounts, Jesus rose from the dead on the
options: third day after His crucifixion
same day as His crucifixion
fortieth day after His crucifixion
seventh day after His crucifixion
questions.explanation: The Gospels consistently record that Jesus rose from the dead on the third day, discovered when women visited His tomb and found it empty.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The empty tomb of Jesus was first discovered by
options: the chief priests and Pharisees
the Roman soldiers guarding the tomb
the eleven remaining disciples together
women, including Mary Magdalene, who had come to anoint His body
questions.explanation: According to the Gospel accounts, women, notably Mary Magdalene, were the first to discover the empty tomb, having come early in the morning to anoint Jesus's body.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Ascension of Jesus refers to the event in which He
options: turned water into wine at a wedding
delivered the Sermon on the Mount
was arrested by the Roman soldiers
was taken up bodily into heaven in the presence of His disciples
questions.explanation: Forty days after His resurrection, Jesus ascended bodily into heaven while His disciples watched, as recorded in Luke and Acts.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Before His Ascension, Jesus gave His disciples what is commonly known as the Great Commission, instructing them to
options: go and make disciples of all nations, baptising and teaching them
build a new temple to replace the one in Jerusalem
remain permanently in Jerusalem without ever leaving
avoid all contact with non-Jewish people
questions.explanation: In the Great Commission (Matthew 28:19-20), Jesus commanded His disciples to spread His teachings to all nations, baptising new believers and teaching them to obey His commands.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Sermon on the Mount, a major body of Jesus's teaching, begins with a series of blessings known as the
options: Ten Commandments
Parables of the Kingdom
Lord's Prayer
Beatitudes
questions.explanation: The Beatitudes (Matthew 5:3-12) open the Sermon on the Mount, pronouncing blessings on qualities such as humility, mercy, and peacemaking.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus taught His followers to pray using the model prayer commonly known as the
options: Lord's Prayer
Prayer of Elijah
Prayer of Solomon
Prayer of Nehemiah
questions.explanation: Jesus taught His disciples the Lord's Prayer as a model for prayer, addressing God as Father and covering praise, provision, forgiveness, and guidance.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Parable of the Sower, one of Jesus's parables of the Kingdom, primarily illustrates
options: the coming destruction of Jerusalem
the importance of financial generosity
the different ways people respond to the message (word) of God
the relationship between Jews and Samaritans
questions.explanation: The Parable of the Sower uses different types of soil to illustrate the varying receptiveness of people's hearts to the message of God's kingdom.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Parable of the Prodigal Son primarily illustrates
options: the importance of hard work in farming
God's readiness to forgive and welcome back a repentant sinner
the proper way to conduct a wedding feast
the dangers of lending money to strangers
questions.explanation: This well-known parable depicts a wayward son who squanders his inheritance but is joyfully welcomed back by his forgiving father, illustrating God's grace toward repentant sinners.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Parable of the Good Samaritan primarily teaches about
options: the dangers of travelling alone
the importance of Temple sacrifices
the qualifications required to become a priest
showing genuine love and compassion to one's neighbour, regardless of ethnic or social background
questions.explanation: In response to the question 'who is my neighbour?', Jesus's parable of the Good Samaritan illustrates that genuine neighbourly love crosses ethnic and social boundaries, exemplified by a despised Samaritan helping an injured stranger.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Jesus's teaching on forgiveness, when Peter asked how many times he should forgive a brother who sinned against him, emphasised
options: forgiving without limit, rather than counting a fixed number of times
forgiving only close family members
never forgiving those who repeatedly sin
forgiving only up to seven times and no more
questions.explanation: When Jesus responded to forgive 'seventy times seven', He was emphasising that forgiveness should be limitless, not a matter of counting a fixed, finite number of offences.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Jesus's teaching concerning wealth, as illustrated in the account of the rich young ruler, warned that
options: material possessions guarantee spiritual blessing
attachment to wealth can be a serious obstacle to fully following God
only the wealthy can enter the Kingdom of God
wealth is always evil and must be entirely rejected by every believer
questions.explanation: When the rich young ruler could not bring himself to give up his wealth to follow Jesus, Jesus used the encounter to warn how difficult it can be for those attached to riches to fully commit to God's kingdom.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Golden Rule, taught by Jesus in the Sermon on the Mount, instructs believers to
options: avoid association with those of different social status
always seek revenge against those who wrong them
do to others what they would want others to do to them
give to the poor only when convenient
questions.explanation: The Golden Rule (Matthew 7:12) summarises a core ethical principle of Jesus's teaching: treating others as one would wish to be treated oneself.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Jesus's teaching on love for one's enemies instructed His followers to
options: seek revenge against anyone who wrongs them
love their enemies and pray for those who persecute them
only show kindness to those who first show kindness to them
avoid all contact with people outside their own community
questions.explanation: In a radical departure from conventional wisdom, Jesus taught His followers to actively love and pray for their enemies, rather than merely tolerating or retaliating against them.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Parable of the Talents primarily teaches about
options: faithful stewardship and responsible use of the gifts and resources God entrusts to individuals
the dangers of travelling to foreign lands
the correct way to conduct a Jewish wedding feast
the importance of building large houses
questions.explanation: The Parable of the Talents illustrates the expectation that believers should faithfully and productively use whatever gifts, opportunities, or resources God has entrusted to them.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Parable of the Lost Sheep primarily illustrates
options: God's great joy in seeking out and finding even a single repentant sinner
the economic value of livestock in ancient Israel
the dangers faced by shepherds in the wilderness
the importance of large flocks for wealth
questions.explanation: This parable depicts a shepherd who leaves ninety-nine sheep to search for one that is lost, illustrating God's deep concern and joy over the recovery of even a single repentant sinner.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Jesus's teaching in the Beatitude 'Blessed are the peacemakers' emphasises that peacemakers
options: shall never face any conflict in life
shall be called children of God
are exempt from all earthly suffering
shall inherit great material wealth
questions.explanation: Among the Beatitudes, Jesus declares that those who actively work to make peace will be recognised and blessed as children of God.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The event known as Pentecost, marking the beginning of the Church, involved
options: the calling of the twelve apostles
the crucifixion of Jesus
the Transfiguration of Jesus
the Holy Spirit descending upon the disciples, enabling them to speak in various languages
questions.explanation: On the day of Pentecost, the Holy Spirit descended upon the gathered disciples with visible signs, empowering them to speak in different languages and marking the birth of the Christian Church.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Following Pentecost, the early believers in Jerusalem were known for their communal life, which included
options: refusing to associate with fellow believers of different backgrounds
living in complete isolation from one another
abandoning all forms of communal worship
sharing their possessions and meeting together regularly for teaching, fellowship, and prayer
questions.explanation: The Book of Acts describes the early church's distinctive communal life, marked by the sharing of resources, devotion to the apostles' teaching, fellowship, breaking of bread, and prayer.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The appointment of the first deacons in the early church, including Stephen, arose mainly to address
options: a disagreement over where to build the first church building
a complaint about the unfair daily distribution of food to widows
a theological dispute about the divinity of Christ
a conflict between the apostles over leadership succession
questions.explanation: The apostles appointed seven men, including Stephen, as deacons specifically to ensure the fair daily distribution of food to widows, resolving a complaint within the growing community.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Stephen, one of the first deacons, became significant in early church history as the first
options: Roman governor to convert to Christianity
Christian martyr, stoned to death for his faith
Gentile convert to Christianity
author of a New Testament epistle
questions.explanation: Stephen was stoned to death by an angry crowd after boldly proclaiming his faith before the Jewish council, making him traditionally regarded as the first Christian martyr.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Apostle Paul's conversion to Christianity occurred while he was travelling to
options: Antioch, to begin his first missionary journey
Damascus, to persecute Christians there
Rome, to stand trial before Caesar
Jerusalem, to be baptised by Peter
questions.explanation: Paul (then known as Saul) experienced a dramatic encounter with the risen Christ on the road to Damascus, where he had been travelling with the intent of persecuting Christians.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Paul's missionary journeys were primarily aimed at
options: spreading the Gospel and establishing new churches among Gentile communities across the Roman Empire
restoring the physical Temple in Jerusalem
conquering foreign territories for Rome
translating the entire Old Testament into Greek
questions.explanation: Paul undertook several extensive missionary journeys throughout the Roman Empire, preaching the Gospel and establishing Christian communities, particularly among Gentile populations.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Council of Jerusalem, described in Acts 15, was convened primarily to address the question of
options: the appointment of a new Roman emperor
the construction of a new temple building
whether Gentile converts to Christianity needed to observe Jewish law, such as circumcision
the exact date on which Easter should be celebrated
questions.explanation: The Council of Jerusalem addressed the significant early controversy over whether Gentile believers needed to adopt Jewish customs like circumcision, ultimately deciding they did not need to fully observe Mosaic law.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Peter played a significant role in opening the Church to Gentile believers through his encounter with the Roman centurion
options: Pontius Pilate
Cornelius
Agrippa
Felix
questions.explanation: Peter's vision and subsequent visit to Cornelius, a Gentile Roman centurion, and the Holy Spirit's evident work in Cornelius's household, was a pivotal moment opening the church's mission to Gentiles.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The early church faced significant persecution, notably under Jewish authorities and later under which Roman emperor known for his brutal persecution of Christians?
options: Julius Caesar
Nero
Augustus
Constantine
questions.explanation: The Roman Emperor Nero is particularly remembered in Christian history for his severe and brutal persecution of Christians, notably following the great fire of Rome.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The growth of the early church, as described in the Book of Acts, is generally attributed to
options: the political enforcement of Christianity by Rome
financial incentives offered to new converts
the power of the Holy Spirit working through the apostles' preaching and the believers' faithful witness
military conquest by Christian armies
questions.explanation: The rapid expansion of the early church is consistently attributed in Acts to the empowering work of the Holy Spirit through bold preaching, miracles, and the faithful witness and unity of believers.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Barnabas played a significant role in the early church mainly by
options: mentoring and vouching for Paul, and later accompanying him on missionary journeys
leading the Jerusalem Council's opposition to Gentile inclusion
serving as the first bishop of Rome
authoring the Gospel of Luke
questions.explanation: Barnabas notably vouched for Paul's genuine conversion to the initially wary apostles and later became a close missionary companion to Paul on his early journeys.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The term 'apostle', used to describe key early Christian leaders like Peter and Paul, generally refers to
options: a member of the Jewish Sanhedrin
one sent out with a specific mission, particularly to spread the Gospel message
a Roman government official
a purely honorary title with no specific responsibility
questions.explanation: The term 'apostle' derives from a word meaning 'one who is sent', referring to those specifically commissioned to spread the Gospel and establish the early Christian church.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Jerusalem Council's final decision regarding Gentile believers, communicated in a letter, asked them to abstain from
options: all forms of manual labour
food sacrificed to idols, blood, meat of strangled animals, and sexual immorality
participating in any form of communal worship
eating meat of any kind whatsoever
questions.explanation: The Council's letter to Gentile believers requested they observe a few key restrictions, without imposing the full burden of Mosaic law, representing an important compromise for church unity.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the overall significance of the Council of Jerusalem for the early church?
options: It abolished the practice of baptism for new converts
It ended all future missionary activity by the apostles
It preserved unity in the church while affirming that salvation is by grace and not dependent on adherence to Jewish law
It led to the permanent division between Jewish and Gentile Christians
questions.explanation: This landmark decision helped preserve unity within the rapidly growing and diversifying early church, affirming that acceptance by God comes through grace and faith rather than strict adherence to Jewish ceremonial law.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Epistle of James places strong emphasis on the relationship between
options: genuine faith and good works, teaching that faith without works is dead
the political organisation of the Roman Empire
the proper structure of Old Testament sacrifices
the exact date of Christ's second coming
questions.explanation: James famously teaches that authentic faith must be demonstrated through corresponding good works, arguing that faith without accompanying action is essentially dead or ineffective.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Epistles of Peter place significant emphasis on believers' civic responsibility, teaching Christians to
options: avoid all interaction with non-believers in society
submit to and respect governing authorities as part of their Christian witness
actively rebel against all forms of civil government
ignore the laws of the state entirely
questions.explanation: Peter's epistles encourage believers to respect and submit to civil authorities as part of living out their faith honourably within society, even under difficult political circumstances.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The virtue of humility, emphasised throughout the New Testament epistles, is best understood as
options: having no confidence or self-worth at all
refusing to ever express one's own opinions
having a modest view of oneself and valuing the needs and interests of others
avoiding any position of leadership or responsibility
questions.explanation: Biblical humility involves a balanced, modest self-assessment combined with genuine regard and concern for the wellbeing and interests of others, rather than self-deprecation or passivity.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Christian virtue of forgiveness, as taught throughout the epistles, is grounded primarily in
options: the idea that forgiveness is unnecessary among true believers
the expectation that wrongdoers must first earn forgiveness through good deeds
the belief that forgiveness should only be extended to family members
the example of God's own forgiveness of believers through Christ
questions.explanation: New Testament teaching consistently roots the Christian obligation to forgive others in the model of God's own gracious forgiveness extended to believers through Christ.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The relationship between faith and works, as discussed in the Epistle of James, is best summarised as
options: true, living faith naturally produces good works as evidence of its genuineness
faith and works are entirely unrelated concepts
good works can exist independently, with no connection to a person's beliefs
works alone are sufficient for salvation, without any need for faith
questions.explanation: James's teaching is best understood not as opposing salvation by faith, but as insisting that authentic, saving faith will inevitably express itself through visible good works.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Civic responsibility, as taught in the epistles concerning Christians and the state, generally includes
options: refusing to pay any taxes to a secular government
avoiding all forms of civic participation entirely
paying taxes, respecting laws, and praying for those in authority
actively working to overthrow all forms of civil government
questions.explanation: New Testament teaching, notably in Romans 13 and 1 Peter 2, encourages believers to fulfil civic duties such as paying taxes, obeying just laws, and praying for governing authorities.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The virtue of faith, as a central theme in the epistles (e.g., Hebrews 11), is best understood as
options: blind acceptance of any claim without careful consideration
confident trust in God and His promises, even without complete physical evidence
reliance solely on one's own abilities and resources
a purely intellectual assent with no impact on behaviour
questions.explanation: Biblical faith, as illustrated by the examples in Hebrews 11, involves a confident trust and reliance on God's character and promises, even when they cannot be fully seen or proven in the present.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Which of the following best summarises the teaching on love found throughout the New Testament epistles?
options: Love is a selfless, active commitment to the wellbeing of others, modelled on Christ's own sacrificial love
Love is primarily an emotional feeling with no practical action required
Love should be reserved exclusively for close family members
Love is optional for genuine believers and not a central Christian virtue
questions.explanation: The epistles, notably 1 Corinthians 13, describe Christian love as a practical, selfless, and active commitment to others' good, deeply rooted in the model of Christ's own sacrificial love.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The application of Christian virtues to statehood and governance, as reflected in the epistles, suggests that believers should
options: seek to establish a Christian government by force
engage responsibly and honourably with civil society while maintaining their ultimate loyalty to God
ignore all ethical considerations when engaging in civic life
completely withdraw from all engagement with civil society and government
questions.explanation: The epistles generally encourage believers to be conscientious, honourable participants in civil society and governance, while always recognising their ultimate allegiance is to God.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Epistle of James also emphasises practical wisdom, teaching believers to be
options: entirely silent in the face of injustice
quick to anger in defence of their beliefs
quick to speak and slow to listen
quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to anger
questions.explanation: James 1:19 offers this well-known practical guidance for believers' conduct in relationships and communication, emphasising patience and restraint in speech and temper.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: After the Flood, God set the rainbow in the sky as a sign of His covenant that He would
options: give Noah dominion over all nations
grant Noah eternal life
always protect Noah's descendants from famine
never again destroy all life on earth by a flood
questions.explanation: Genesis 9:12-16 records the rainbow as the sign of God's covenant promise never again to destroy the earth by a flood.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: God's covenant with Noah after the Flood was made with
options: only the nation of Israel
Noah, his descendants, and every living creature on earth
only Noah and his three sons
only the animals that survived the flood
questions.explanation: Genesis 9:9-10 specifies that God's covenant was established with Noah, his offspring, and every living creature that came out of the ark.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: In His covenant with Abraham, God promised to
options: make him king over Egypt
grant him the throne of Israel
give him victory over the Philistines
make him a great nation and give his descendants the land of Canaan
questions.explanation: Genesis 12 and 15 record God's covenant promises to Abraham of numerous descendants and the land of Canaan as an inheritance.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The sign God gave Abraham as the mark of His covenant was
options: the building of an altar in Canaan
circumcision of every male
the offering of a lamb each year
the wearing of special garments
questions.explanation: Genesis 17:10-11 establishes circumcision as the physical sign of the covenant between God and Abraham's descendants.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: God tested Abraham's faith and obedience by commanding him to
options: fight against the kings who captured Lot
offer his son Isaac as a sacrifice on a mountain in Moriah
leave his homeland without any provision
give up all his flocks and herds
questions.explanation: Genesis 22 recounts God testing Abraham by commanding him to sacrifice Isaac, though God provided a ram as a substitute at the last moment.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: At Bethel, Jacob had a vision of
options: a chariot of fire taking Elijah to heaven
a burning bush that was not consumed
a valley full of dry bones
a ladder reaching to heaven with angels ascending and descending
questions.explanation: Genesis 28:12 describes Jacob's dream at Bethel of a ladder connecting earth to heaven, with angels moving upon it, after which God renewed the covenant promise to him.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Jacob's name was changed to Israel after he
options: reconciled with his uncle Laban
wrestled all night with a divine being at Peniel
defeated his brother Esau in battle
built an altar at Bethel
questions.explanation: Genesis 32:24-28 describes Jacob wrestling until daybreak with a divine being, after which his name was changed to Israel, meaning 'he struggles with God'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: While imprisoned in Egypt, Joseph correctly interpreted the dreams of
options: Pharaoh himself
Pharaoh's cupbearer and baker
his own brothers
the captain of the guard
questions.explanation: Genesis 40 records Joseph interpreting the dreams of Pharaoh's imprisoned cupbearer and baker, correctly predicting the restoration of one and the execution of the other.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: When Joseph finally revealed his identity to his brothers in Egypt, he told them not to be distressed because
options: Pharaoh had ordered their release from guilt
he had already forgiven their father Jacob
God had sent him ahead of them to preserve life during the famine
he no longer considered them his brothers
questions.explanation: In Genesis 45:5-8, Joseph reassures his brothers that God used their actions for good, sending him ahead to preserve many lives during the famine.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The ten plagues that God brought upon Egypt were primarily intended to
options: test the faith of the Israelites
punish the Egyptians for building the pyramids
destroy Egypt's agriculture permanently
compel Pharaoh to let the Israelites leave Egyptian slavery
questions.explanation: Exodus 7-12 describes the plagues as God's judgement on Egypt and the means by which Pharaoh was ultimately compelled to release the Israelites from slavery.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: During the first Passover in Egypt, the Israelites were instructed to apply the blood of a lamb to their doorposts so that
options: the plague of death on the firstborn would pass over their houses
the Nile would not turn to blood in their homes
the Egyptians would recognise them as slaves
they would be protected from the plague of locusts
questions.explanation: Exodus 12:13 explains that the lamb's blood on the doorposts served as a sign for the Lord to pass over Israelite homes during the final plague, sparing their firstborn.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: As the Israelites fled Egypt, God enabled them to cross the sea by
options: guiding them around the sea entirely
causing the sea to freeze over
dividing the waters so they could cross on dry ground
providing boats for the entire nation
questions.explanation: Exodus 14:21-22 describes God parting the Red Sea through a strong east wind, allowing the Israelites to cross on dry ground while the pursuing Egyptian army was later destroyed.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: In the wilderness, God provided the Israelites with daily food in the form of
options: milk and honey directly from heaven
manna and quail
figs and olives
bread and wine
questions.explanation: Exodus 16 records God's provision of manna each morning and quail for the wandering Israelites in the wilderness.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: At Mount Sinai, God established His covenant with Israel by giving Moses
options: the Ten Commandments as the foundation of the law
the names of the twelve tribes
the plans for the Ark of the Covenant only
a new set of sacrificial animals
questions.explanation: Exodus 20 records God giving Moses the Ten Commandments at Mount Sinai, forming the core of the covenant law between God and Israel.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: While Moses was on Mount Sinai receiving the law, the Israelites persuaded Aaron to make
options: a bronze serpent for healing
a golden calf for them to worship
a new altar for sacrifices
a copy of the Ark of the Covenant
questions.explanation: Exodus 32 describes how the impatient Israelites pressured Aaron into fashioning a golden calf, which they worshipped in violation of the covenant they had just made with God.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Ark of the Covenant, central to Israel's worship, primarily housed
options: the rod that turned into a serpent
the tablets of the Ten Commandments
the bones of Joseph
Aaron's priestly garments
questions.explanation: The Ark of the Covenant primarily contained the stone tablets of the Ten Commandments, symbolising God's presence and covenant with Israel (Exodus 25:16).

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: When Moses sent twelve spies to explore Canaan, only two of them - Caleb and Joshua - urged the people to
options: wait another forty years before entering Canaan
build permanent settlements in the wilderness
return immediately to Egypt
trust God and proceed to take possession of the land
questions.explanation: Numbers 13-14 records that while ten spies gave a discouraging report, Caleb and Joshua alone urged Israel to trust God's promise and take the land.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Rahab of Jericho assisted the Israelite conquest of Canaan by
options: leading the Israelite army into the city
warning King Ahab of the coming invasion
hiding the two spies sent by Joshua and helping them escape
providing food for the wandering Israelites
questions.explanation: Joshua 2 records how Rahab hid the two Israelite spies in Jericho and helped them escape, in exchange for the promise of safety for her family.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Deborah, the only female judge mentioned in the Bible, led Israel to victory over Canaanite forces alongside the military commander
options: Gideon
Othniel
Ehud
Barak
questions.explanation: Judges 4 describes Deborah, a prophetess and judge, summoning Barak to lead Israel's army against Sisera's Canaanite forces, resulting in victory.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Canaanite general Sisera, defeated in battle in the time of Deborah, was ultimately killed by
options: Deborah herself
Gideon's soldiers
Jael, who drove a tent peg through his temple
Barak, in single combat
questions.explanation: Judges 4:21 records that Jael killed the fleeing Sisera by driving a tent peg through his temple while he slept in her tent.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Samuel's mother, Hannah, dedicated him to the Lord's service after
options: being instructed by the priest Eli to do so
praying fervently for a son and vowing to give him to God
receiving a direct command through a burning bush
losing all her other children
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 1 recounts Hannah's earnest prayer for a son and her vow to dedicate him to the Lord's service, a vow she fulfilled after Samuel's birth.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: As a boy serving in the temple under the priest Eli, Samuel first received God's call
options: while tending sheep in the fields
through a dream about seven years of famine
at night, hearing his name called until Eli helped him recognise it was the Lord
through a vision of a ladder to heaven
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 3 describes young Samuel hearing his name called repeatedly at night, until Eli discerned it was the Lord and instructed Samuel how to respond.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: David's close friendship with Jonathan, Saul's son, was marked especially by
options: constant rivalry over the throne of Israel
a shared plot to overthrow Saul
Jonathan's refusal to ever help David
a covenant of loyalty, with Jonathan protecting David from Saul's anger
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 18-20 describes the deep covenant friendship between David and Jonathan, with Jonathan repeatedly protecting David from Saul's murderous jealousy.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The prophet Nathan confronted David over his sin with Bathsheba by telling a parable about
options: a rich man who stole a poor man's only lamb
a shepherd who lost one of a hundred sheep
a servant who was forgiven a great debt
a farmer who scattered seed on different soils
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12 records Nathan's parable of a rich man who took a poor man's beloved ewe lamb, which exposed David's guilt regarding Uriah and Bathsheba.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: At the dedication of the newly built Temple, Solomon's prayer chiefly
options: requested victory over all of Israel's remaining enemies
asked for the restoration of the tribes lost to Egypt
sought forgiveness for his father David's sins alone
asked God to hear the prayers of His people offered towards the Temple
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 8 records Solomon's dedicatory prayer asking that God would hear and answer the prayers of Israel and even foreigners directed towards the Temple.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: King Ahab's desire for Naboth's vineyard led to Naboth's death after Queen Jezebel
options: bribed Naboth's own sons to kill him
sent soldiers to attack Naboth's family directly
poisoned Naboth's food
arranged false witnesses to accuse Naboth of blasphemy so he could be stoned
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 21 recounts how Jezebel orchestrated false accusations of blasphemy against Naboth, leading to his stoning so Ahab could seize his vineyard.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Elisha became Elijah's successor as prophet after
options: Elijah's mantle fell to him as Elijah was taken up to heaven in a whirlwind
he built the second Temple
he was anointed by King Ahab
he defeated the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 2 describes Elisha receiving Elijah's mantle, symbolising his succession, as Elijah was taken up to heaven in a whirlwind with a chariot of fire.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Elisha's servant Gehazi was struck with leprosy as punishment for
options: worshipping Baal in secret
stealing from a widow's jar of oil
refusing to serve Elisha any longer
deceitfully accepting silver and garments from Naaman after Elisha had refused any payment
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:20-27 recounts Gehazi's greedy deception of Naaman for silver and clothing, for which Elisha pronounced that Naaman's leprosy would cling to Gehazi and his descendants.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Syrian commander Naaman was healed of his leprosy after he
options: obeyed Elisha's instruction to dip seven times in the Jordan River
fasted for forty days in the wilderness
offered a great sacrifice at the Temple in Jerusalem
was anointed with oil by the king of Israel
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5 records that Naaman was healed of leprosy only after reluctantly obeying Elisha's instruction to wash seven times in the Jordan River.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The prophet Elijah's earthly life ended when he was
options: killed by King Ahab's soldiers
buried honourably in Jerusalem
stoned to death by the people of Israel
taken up to heaven in a whirlwind by a chariot of fire
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 2:11 describes Elijah being taken up into heaven in a whirlwind, with a chariot and horses of fire appearing before Elisha.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: King Josiah's religious reforms in Judah were sparked chiefly by the discovery of
options: the Ark of the Covenant, long thought lost
a vision given directly to Josiah in a dream
a letter from the prophet Jeremiah
the Book of the Law during repairs to the Temple
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22 records that Josiah's sweeping reforms began after the Book of the Law was discovered during Temple repairs, prompting national repentance.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: As part of his reforms, King Josiah restored the observance of
options: circumcision, which had been entirely forgotten
the Feast of Tabernacles for the first time in Israel's history
the offering of firstfruits, previously unknown in Israel
the Passover, celebrated on a scale not seen since the days of the judges
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 23:21-23 records Josiah's restoration of the Passover celebration on an unprecedented scale, following his removal of idolatrous practices from Judah.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The fall of Jerusalem and the beginning of the Babylonian exile occurred during the reign of
options: Solomon, at the height of his wealth
Hezekiah, following an Assyrian invasion
Josiah, shortly after his reforms
Zedekiah, the last king of Judah
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25 records that Jerusalem fell to the Babylonians and the Temple was destroyed during the reign of Zedekiah, Judah's last king, marking the start of the exile.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: When God called Jonah to preach against the wickedness of Nineveh, Jonah initially responded by
options: obeying immediately without hesitation
fleeing in the opposite direction by ship toward Tarshish
preaching a message of destruction without any warning
asking God to send someone else instead
questions.explanation: Jonah 1:3 records that instead of obeying God's call to Nineveh, Jonah attempted to flee by sea toward Tarshish, in the opposite direction.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: After being thrown overboard during a storm, Jonah was
options: swallowed by a great fish and remained inside it for three days and three nights
washed ashore immediately near Nineveh
drowned as punishment for his disobedience
rescued by sailors who turned back for him
questions.explanation: Jonah 1:17 describes God providing a great fish to swallow Jonah, who remained inside it for three days and nights before being brought to dry land.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: When Jonah finally delivered God's message to Nineveh, the city's response was to
options: repent in sackcloth and fasting, from the king down to the common people
ignore the warning entirely, resulting in the city's destruction
kill Jonah for prophesying against them
reject the message and expel Jonah from the city
questions.explanation: Jonah 3 records the remarkable repentance of Nineveh, with the king and all the people fasting and turning from their evil ways in response to Jonah's warning.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Jonah became angry after God spared Nineveh because
options: God had not fulfilled a separate promise made to him
the people of Nineveh had mocked him publicly
he had been promised a reward for their destruction
he resented God's mercy being extended to Israel's enemies
questions.explanation: Jonah 4 reveals that Jonah was displeased and angry precisely because God's compassionate mercy spared Nineveh, a nation Jonah considered Israel's enemy.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: In one of his visions, Amos saw the Lord standing beside a wall holding a
options: burning fire consuming the land
basket of ripe fruit, symbolising that the end had come
swarm of locusts devouring the crops
plumb line, symbolising God's standard of judgement for Israel
questions.explanation: Amos 7:7-9 describes the vision of the plumb line, symbolising that Israel would be measured against God's standard of righteousness and found wanting.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Amos's famous call for justice declared that it should
options: 'be established only through Temple sacrifices'
'roll down like waters, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream'
'wait until the coming of the Messiah'
'be administered solely by the king's court'
questions.explanation: Amos 5:24 contains this well-known declaration demanding genuine justice and righteousness rather than empty religious ritual.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: God commanded the prophet Hosea to marry
options: Gomer, a woman characterised by unfaithfulness, as a living illustration of Israel's relationship with God
a widow, in order to provide for her financially
a foreign princess to seal a political alliance
a woman from the tribe of Levi only
questions.explanation: Hosea 1:2 records God's command that Hosea marry Gomer, whose unfaithfulness would mirror Israel's spiritual unfaithfulness to God.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The prophet Micah summarised what the Lord requires of His people as
options: to act justly, love mercy, and walk humbly with God
to build grand temples in every city
to conquer surrounding nations militarily
to offer burnt offerings and sacrifices continually
questions.explanation: Micah 6:8 famously summarises true religion as acting justly, loving mercy, and walking humbly with God, above mere ritual sacrifice.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Isaiah's prophecy of the 'suffering servant' describes one who would be
options: exalted immediately without any suffering
crowned as an earthly conquering king
sent to destroy Israel's enemies by military force
wounded for the transgressions of others and bear their sins
questions.explanation: Isaiah 53 describes the suffering servant who would be pierced and wounded for the transgressions of others, a passage Christians understand as pointing to Christ.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Isaiah's prophecy that 'a virgin shall conceive and bear a son' names the child
options: Emmanuel Josiah
Jedidiah
Melchizedek
Immanuel, meaning 'God with us'
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:14 gives the child the name Immanuel, meaning 'God with us', a prophecy Christians associate with the birth of Jesus in Matthew 1:23.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: During a severe drought, God provided for the prophet Elijah at the Kerith Ravine through
options: an angel who cooked food for him
a widow who fed him from her own storeroom in Jerusalem
manna falling from heaven each morning
ravens that brought him bread and meat
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 17:4-6 describes God commanding ravens to bring Elijah bread and meat morning and evening while he hid at the Kerith Ravine.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The prophet Elisha performed a notable miracle for a Shunammite woman by
options: multiplying her jar of oil to pay off her debts
raising her son back to life after he had died
healing her of a lifelong illness
giving her husband a prophetic dream
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 4 records Elisha raising the Shunammite woman's son back to life after the boy had died suddenly, in reward for her earlier hospitality to the prophet.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Jesus called His first disciples, Peter and Andrew, while they were
options: tending sheep in the fields near Bethlehem
casting their nets into the Sea of Galilee as fishermen
collecting taxes at a toll booth
worshipping in the synagogue at Capernaum
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:18-19 records Jesus calling Peter and Andrew as they cast their nets into the sea, promising to make them 'fishers of men'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Jesus performed His first recorded miracle at a wedding in Cana by
options: healing the bridegroom's servant
turning water into wine
multiplying loaves and fishes
calming a sudden storm
questions.explanation: John 2:1-11 describes Jesus turning water into wine at a wedding in Cana of Galilee, described as the first of His miraculous signs.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: When Nicodemus, a Pharisee, came to Jesus at night, Jesus taught him that a person must
options: offer sacrifices continually at the Temple
keep the entire Mosaic law perfectly
be born again to see the Kingdom of God
become a member of the Sanhedrin
questions.explanation: John 3:3 records Jesus's teaching to Nicodemus that spiritual rebirth is essential for entering the Kingdom of God.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: At Jacob's well, Jesus spoke with a Samaritan woman and revealed to her that
options: only Jews could receive the water of life
He was the Messiah she was waiting for
she needed to travel to Jerusalem to worship properly
she must first convert fully to Judaism
questions.explanation: John 4:25-26 records Jesus explicitly identifying Himself as the Messiah to the Samaritan woman, also teaching that true worship is in spirit and truth, not tied to a specific location.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Jesus fed a crowd of about five thousand people using
options: five loaves of bread and two fish
manna that fell from heaven
seven loaves and a few small fish
twelve baskets of grain
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:13-21 records Jesus multiplying five loaves and two fish to feed the crowd, with twelve baskets of leftovers gathered afterward.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: During a night storm on the Sea of Galilee, Jesus demonstrated His power over nature by
options: creating a bridge of ice across the sea
walking on the water toward His disciples' boat
summoning a rescue boat from the shore
causing the boat to fly above the waves
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:25-33 describes Jesus walking on the water to reach His disciples' boat during a storm, also enabling Peter briefly to walk on water toward Him.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: When a violent storm threatened to sink the disciples' boat, Jesus calmed it by
options: instructing the disciples to row harder
rebuking the wind and saying to the sea, 'Peace, be still'
praying silently until the storm passed naturally
throwing cargo overboard to stabilise the boat
questions.explanation: Mark 4:39 records Jesus rebuking the wind and commanding the sea to be still, immediately producing a great calm and amazing His disciples.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: A paralysed man was healed by Jesus after his friends brought him to Jesus by
options: leaving him at the Pool of Bethesda
bringing him to the synagogue on the Sabbath
lowering him through a hole made in the roof because of the crowd
carrying him on a stretcher through the front door
questions.explanation: Mark 2:1-12 describes friends lowering a paralysed man through a roof opening to reach Jesus, who both forgave his sins and healed him.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: When a man with leprosy approached Jesus for healing, Jesus responded by
options: sending him directly to the priests without healing him first
instructing him to wash seven times in the Jordan
refusing to touch him but healing him from a distance
touching him and declaring 'Be clean', instantly healing him
questions.explanation: Mark 1:40-42 records Jesus compassionately touching the leper and healing him immediately, then instructing him to show himself to the priest as the law required.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: A Roman centurion's faith impressed Jesus when he said that Jesus need only
options: offer a sacrifice on the servant's behalf
pray publicly in the synagogue for the servant
'say the word' for his servant to be healed, without needing to visit in person
come and lay hands physically on the servant
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:8-10 records the centurion's remarkable faith that Jesus could heal simply by speaking a word, which Jesus praised as greater than any faith found in Israel.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Jesus demonstrated His power over death by raising Lazarus, who had already
options: died of an illness Jesus had failed to prevent
just died moments earlier
been dead and in the tomb for four days
been declared dead but was merely unconscious
questions.explanation: John 11:39-44 records that Lazarus had been in the tomb four days before Jesus called him back to life, demonstrating His power even over decay and death.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Jairus, a synagogue leader, sought Jesus's help because
options: his household had been struck by famine
his young daughter was dying and later died before Jesus arrived
his wife had been afflicted with a bleeding disorder
his son had been possessed by an unclean spirit
questions.explanation: Mark 5:22-24, 35-42 records Jairus pleading for his dying daughter, who died before Jesus arrived but whom Jesus then raised back to life.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: At the town of Nain, Jesus was moved with compassion and raised to life
options: the only son of a widow, during his funeral procession
the daughter of a synagogue ruler
his friend Lazarus
