a beggar who had died at the town gate
questions.explanation: Luke 7:11-15 describes Jesus encountering a funeral procession for a widow's only son at Nain and raising the young man back to life out of compassion for his mother.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: When Martha complained that her sister Mary was not helping with household tasks, Jesus responded that Mary had
options: been wrong to neglect her domestic duties
been told to immediately return to help Martha
been favoured unfairly over her sister
chosen the better part by sitting and listening to His teaching
questions.explanation: Luke 10:38-42 records Jesus gently correcting Martha's anxiety, affirming that Mary's choice to sit and listen to His teaching was the 'better part'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Parable of the Unforgiving Servant teaches that believers who have been forgiven by God should
options: likewise forgive others who owe them a debt or wrong
avoid lending to others altogether
demand full repayment from those who wrong them
only forgive those who ask multiple times
questions.explanation: Matthew 18:23-35 tells of a servant forgiven a huge debt who refused to forgive a much smaller debt owed to him, illustrating the necessity of forgiving others as God forgives us.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Parable of the Ten Virgins (bridesmaids) primarily teaches the importance of
options: being spiritually prepared and watchful for the Lord's coming
sharing resources generously with others
the proper customs of a Jewish wedding
showing hospitality to wedding guests
questions.explanation: Matthew 25:1-13 tells of five wise virgins who kept extra oil for their lamps and five foolish ones who did not, teaching believers to remain spiritually prepared for Christ's return.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: In the Parable of the Pharisee and the Tax Collector, the tax collector was justified before God because he
options: listed his good deeds before God in prayer
offered a large sacrifice at the Temple
humbly acknowledged his sinfulness and asked for God's mercy
compared himself favourably to the Pharisee
questions.explanation: Luke 18:9-14 contrasts the self-righteous Pharisee with the humble tax collector, whose simple prayer for mercy resulted in him being justified rather than the Pharisee.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Parable of the Mustard Seed illustrates that the Kingdom of God
options: will never expand beyond Israel
requires great wealth to establish
is hidden permanently from human understanding
begins small but grows into something great
questions.explanation: Matthew 13:31-32 compares the Kingdom of God to a tiny mustard seed that grows into a large tree, illustrating its small beginnings and eventual great expansion.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Parable of the Workers in the Vineyard illustrates that
options: God's grace is generous and not based on human notions of fairness regarding effort
only the first workers hired deserve a full wage
workers should always be paid strictly according to hours worked
landowners should exploit workers for maximum profit
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:1-16 tells of a landowner who pays all workers the same wage regardless of when they were hired, illustrating the generosity of God's grace beyond human standards of fairness.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Parable of the Rich Fool warns against
options: the dangers of farming without proper planning
storing up earthly wealth while neglecting one's relationship with God
refusing to build barns for one's harvest
lending money to those who cannot repay
questions.explanation: Luke 12:16-21 tells of a rich man who built bigger barns to store his abundant harvest but died that very night, illustrating the folly of prioritising wealth over readiness to meet God.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: In the Parable of the Great Banquet (Wedding Feast), those originally invited who refused to come represent
options: those who reject God's invitation, making way for others, including outcasts, to be invited
the priests who administered the Temple sacrifices
the Gentile nations who never received an invitation
the faithful remnant who alone will enter the Kingdom
questions.explanation: Luke 14:15-24 tells of invited guests who make excuses and refuse to attend, so the host instead invites the poor, crippled, and marginalised, illustrating the rejection of God's invitation by some and its extension to others.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: At Caesarea Philippi, Peter famously declared to Jesus,
options: 'You are the King of the Jews'
'You are the Christ, the Son of the living God'
'You are a great prophet like Moses'
'You are Elijah returned to earth'
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:16 records Peter's confession at Caesarea Philippi, recognising Jesus as the Christ, the Son of the living God.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: When asked which was the greatest commandment, Jesus replied that it was to
options: observe the Sabbath without exception
love the Lord with all one's heart, soul, and mind, and love one's neighbour as oneself
obey the Roman civil authorities without question
offer sacrifices continually at the Temple
questions.explanation: Matthew 22:37-39 records Jesus summarising the entire law and prophets in the twin commandments to love God completely and to love one's neighbour as oneself.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Jesus expressed righteous anger by overturning tables in the Temple courts because
options: the Pharisees had removed the Ark of the Covenant
the Temple had not been rebuilt after the exile
the priests had refused Him entry
merchants and money changers had turned a house of prayer into a den of thieves
questions.explanation: Matthew 21:12-13 records Jesus driving out the merchants and money changers, declaring that they had turned God's house of prayer into a den of robbers.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: During Jesus's trial, Peter denied knowing Jesus
options: never, remaining faithful throughout the trial
only after being tortured by Roman soldiers
three times before the rooster crowed, just as Jesus had predicted
once, before quickly being arrested himself
questions.explanation: Matthew 26:69-75 records Peter denying Jesus three times in the courtyard before the rooster crowed, fulfilling Jesus's earlier prediction.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Before His crucifixion, Jesus was brought before the Jewish council (Sanhedrin), presided over by the high priest
options: Annas alone
Herod Antipas
Pontius Pilate
Caiaphas
questions.explanation: Matthew 26:57 records that Jesus was brought before Caiaphas, the high priest, and the assembled Sanhedrin, where He was accused of blasphemy.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The disciple Thomas initially refused to believe Jesus had risen until he
options: heard testimony from all the other disciples together
received a direct vision from an angel
could see and touch the wounds in Jesus's hands and side
saw Jesus ascend into heaven
questions.explanation: John 20:24-28 records Thomas's insistence on physically seeing and touching Jesus's wounds before believing, until Jesus appeared and invited him to do so.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: On the road to Emmaus, two disciples recognised the risen Jesus when He
options: broke bread with them at the table
ascended before their eyes
called them each by name
revealed the nail marks in His hands
questions.explanation: Luke 24:30-31 describes the two disciples' eyes being opened to recognise the risen Jesus at the moment He broke bread with them.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The apostle Philip led an Ethiopian court official to faith in Christ by
options: translating the Torah into his native language
performing a miraculous sign before him
healing him of a physical ailment
explaining that the prophecy of Isaiah 53 the eunuch was reading pointed to Jesus
questions.explanation: Acts 8:26-38 records Philip explaining that the suffering servant passage in Isaiah 53 pointed to Jesus, leading the Ethiopian eunuch to believe and be baptised.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Ananias and Sapphira died suddenly in the early church after
options: publicly denying their faith in Christ
lying to the Holy Spirit about the amount they received from selling their property
opposing the apostles' preaching in the Temple
refusing to share any of their possessions with the church
questions.explanation: Acts 5:1-10 recounts how Ananias and Sapphira died after deceitfully claiming to give the full proceeds of a land sale while secretly withholding part of it, thereby lying to the Holy Spirit.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Apostle Paul's teaching in Romans that a person is justified by faith means that
options: one is made right with God through faith in Christ, not by works of the law
good works alone are sufficient for salvation
salvation is earned entirely through obedience to the Mosaic law
only Jewish believers can be justified before God
questions.explanation: Romans 3:28 and 5:1 teach that justification (being declared righteous before God) comes through faith in Christ rather than through works of the law.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: In Romans 6, Paul answers the question 'Shall we go on sinning so that grace may increase?' by declaring
options: 'By no means! We died to sin; how can we live in it any longer?'
'Yes, since grace covers every sin regardless of behaviour'
'Only if one has never been baptised'
'It does not matter, since the law has been abolished'
questions.explanation: Romans 6:1-2 has Paul emphatically rejecting the idea that grace is a licence to continue sinning, since believers have died to sin through their union with Christ.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Paul's declaration in Romans 8:1 assures believers that
options: all believers must still fear final judgement equally with unbelievers
condemnation is avoided only through continual sacrifice
the law remains the only path to acceptance with God
there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus
questions.explanation: Romans 8:1 offers this foundational assurance of freedom from condemnation for those united with Christ, a cornerstone of New Testament teaching on grace.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Paul's teaching on spiritual gifts in 1 Corinthians 12 emphasises that
options: spiritual gifts are reserved only for apostles
only the gift of tongues indicates genuine faith
every believer must possess the identical spiritual gift
the gifts are diverse but come from the same Spirit, given for the common good of the church
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:4-7 teaches that though spiritual gifts vary widely, they originate from the same Spirit and are given to benefit the whole church community.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Paul's metaphor of the church as 'the body of Christ' in 1 Corinthians 12 illustrates that
options: only certain believers are truly essential to the church
each believer functions entirely independently of others
believers, though different in function, are interdependent members of one unified body
the church should be organised like a strict hierarchy of authority
questions.explanation: Paul uses the analogy of a human body with many interdependent parts to illustrate the unity-in-diversity of believers functioning together as the body of Christ.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Paul concludes his famous discourse on love in 1 Corinthians 13 by declaring that of faith, hope, and love,
options: faith is superior to the other two
the greatest of these is love
all three are of exactly equal significance with no priority
hope will ultimately replace both faith and love
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 13:13 concludes that while faith, hope, and love all endure, love is declared the greatest of the three virtues.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Paul's teaching on Christian giving in 2 Corinthians 9 emphasises that believers should give
options: cheerfully and not reluctantly or under compulsion
solely to fellow believers within their own local congregation
only the exact tenth required under the Mosaic law
only when they have surplus wealth remaining
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 9:7 teaches that God loves a cheerful giver, encouraging believers to give generously and willingly rather than out of reluctance or compulsion.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: According to Galatians 5, the fruit of the Spirit includes
options: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control
wealth, health, and worldly success
wisdom, knowledge, prophecy, tongues, and miracles
strict adherence to circumcision and dietary laws
questions.explanation: Galatians 5:22-23 lists the fruit of the Spirit as these nine Christlike character qualities that grow in a believer's life through the Holy Spirit.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: In Ephesians 6, Paul instructs believers to put on the 'full armour of God' primarily in order to
options: prepare for literal warfare against Israel's enemies
protect themselves from physical illness
defend themselves against Roman soldiers
stand firm against the schemes of the devil in spiritual conflict
questions.explanation: Ephesians 6:11-13 uses the imagery of a soldier's armour to describe the spiritual resources believers need to withstand the devil's schemes.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Paul's appeal for unity in Ephesians 4 urges believers to maintain
options: the unity of the Spirit through the bond of peace
strict uniformity in every personal opinion
competition to determine the most important members
separation between different spiritual gift bearers
questions.explanation: Ephesians 4:3 calls believers to make every effort to keep the unity of the Spirit through the bond of peace, despite their diversity of gifts and backgrounds.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Philippians 2 describes the humility of Christ, who, though He was in the form of God,
options: refused to associate with sinners or outcasts
emptied Himself, taking the form of a servant, and humbled Himself to death on a cross
demanded worship from all people during His earthly life
avoided suffering entirely during His ministry
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:6-8 describes Christ's profound humility in emptying Himself of His divine privileges, taking on human form, and submitting even to death on a cross.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Paul's teaching on contentment in Philippians 4 states that he has learned to be content
options: solely while he was imprisoned for the gospel
by depending entirely on the generosity of others
only when his material needs are fully met
in whatever circumstances he finds himself, through Christ who strengthens him
questions.explanation: Philippians 4:11-13 records Paul's testimony that he learned contentment in every circumstance, relying on the strength Christ provides.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Colossians 1 describes Christ as
options: the image of the invisible God, in whom all things were created and hold together
merely one of many prophets sent by God
a created being subordinate to the angels
only significant for His earthly moral teaching
questions.explanation: Colossians 1:15-17 presents an exalted view of Christ as the image of the invisible God, through whom and for whom all things were created, and in whom all things hold together.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Paul's teaching on the Lord's return in 1 Thessalonians 4 describes believers who are alive at Christ's coming as being
options: required to die before entering the Kingdom
left behind to endure further tribulation alone
caught up together with the risen dead to meet the Lord in the air
unaware of any change occurring at all
questions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 4:16-17 describes the dead in Christ rising first, followed by living believers being caught up together with them to meet the Lord in the air.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Paul warns in 1 Thessalonians 5 that the Day of the Lord will come
options: like a thief in the night, unexpectedly
only after a long period of visible warning signs
at a precisely predictable, calculated date
exclusively upon unbelieving Gentile nations
questions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:2 warns that the Day of the Lord will arrive suddenly and unexpectedly, like a thief in the night, urging believers to remain spiritually alert.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: In 1 Timothy 3, Paul outlines the qualifications for overseers (elders) in the church, requiring that they be
options: unmarried, so as to devote themselves fully to ministry
above reproach, faithful to one wife, self-controlled, and able to teach
recent converts, to bring fresh perspective to leadership
wealthy landowners with significant social standing
questions.explanation: 1 Timothy 3:1-7 lists the moral and character qualifications required of church overseers, including being above reproach, faithful in marriage, and able to teach sound doctrine.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Paul encourages Timothy to endure hardship as a Christian minister by comparing him to
options: a king ruling without opposition
a good soldier of Christ Jesus who does not get entangled in civilian affairs
a farmer who need not work hard for a harvest
a merchant seeking easy profit
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 2:3-4 uses the image of a soldier single-mindedly devoted to his commanding officer to encourage Timothy's steadfast endurance in ministry.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Paul's teaching to Timothy regarding Scripture affirms that
options: only the words of Jesus in the Gospels carry divine authority
Scripture is a purely human record with no divine origin
all Scripture is God-breathed and useful for teaching, rebuking, correcting, and training in righteousness
the Old Testament law has no further relevance for believers
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 3:16 affirms the divine inspiration and practical usefulness of Scripture for teaching, correction, and equipping believers for righteous living.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: In his letter to Philemon, Paul appeals on behalf of
options: Timothy, requesting his release from prison
Onesimus, a runaway slave, urging Philemon to receive him back as a brother in Christ
Titus, seeking his appointment as a bishop
the church at Colossae, requesting financial support
questions.explanation: Paul's short letter to Philemon pleads for the runaway slave Onesimus to be welcomed back not merely as a slave but as a beloved brother in Christ.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Epistle to the Hebrews describes Jesus as
options: one who never faced any form of temptation
a priest inferior to the Levitical priesthood
a figure entirely separate from the Old Testament sacrificial system
a great high priest who sympathises with human weakness, having been tempted in every way
questions.explanation: Hebrews 4:14-15 presents Jesus as a great high priest who, though without sin, can sympathise with human weaknesses because He was tempted in every way as we are.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Hebrews 11, often called the 'faith chapter', commends Noah for his faith because he
options: built an ark to save his family, though he had never seen a flood before
led Israel out of Egyptian slavery
left his homeland without knowing his destination
offered his son Isaac as a sacrifice
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:7 commends Noah's faith in building the ark in obedience to God's warning about things not yet seen, resulting in the salvation of his household.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: First Peter encourages believers facing persecution by teaching that
options: believers should retaliate against their persecutors
suffering for doing good, when it is God's will, is better than suffering for doing wrong
suffering indicates a lack of genuine faith
true faith guarantees a life free from all suffering
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 3:17 teaches that it is better, if it is God's will, to suffer for doing good than for doing evil, encouraging perseverance in righteous conduct despite persecution.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Second Peter warns the church chiefly about the danger of
options: false teachers who would secretly introduce destructive heresies
excessive generosity toward the poor
the return of Old Testament dietary laws
abandoning fellowship with other believers
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 2:1 warns that, just as there were false prophets among the people of Israel, false teachers would arise within the church, secretly introducing destructive heresies.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Apostle John's first epistle declares that believers can know and demonstrate the truth of the gospel because
options: only apostles were capable of truly loving others
love is merely a human emotion unrelated to faith
love is optional in the Christian life
God is love, and this love is revealed by sending His Son so that we might live through Him
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:8-9 declares that God is love, made manifest in sending His Son so that believers might live through Him.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: First John assures believers that
options: only public confession before the entire church leads to forgiveness
confession of sin is unnecessary once a person becomes a believer
if we confess our sins, God is faithful and just to forgive us and cleanse us from all unrighteousness
sins committed after conversion can never be forgiven
questions.explanation: 1 John 1:9 offers this well-known assurance that confessing sin results in God's faithful and just forgiveness and cleansing.
